reviews.comment: Be prepared for the unnecessary lectures that don't touch up fully on the assigned readings we had in class. He ends up using the entire class period to talk more about philosophical ideals. Has hard participation grades, will cut you off when speaking, or rant so much that you can't get a word in. I would avoid this professor if you want to learn.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I was going to apply to TAMU's English MA until I learned that DiCaglio was the grad director. His lectures are rambling and incoherent as he usually just says what not to do instead of actually explaining concepts. He was annoyed when students asked questions and when he had take time out of his 'admin day' to explain concepts in office hours.
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Took this class fall of '22 would not recommend at all. Hard grader with little to no effective feedback. When a student doesn't understand the material or feedback, they were instructed to think differently and he would get visibly frustrated if students didn't agree. Not a bad guy, extremely unorganized lectures, and hard grading.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Dicaglio encourages students to embrace an entirely new way of thinking about the world in this course-- one that requires high-level thinking. Initially, I found his lecture style to be really difficult to navigate, but it started to make more sense after a few weeks. After this course, you will look at rhetoric in an entirely different way.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. DiCaglio is different. He's clearly very smart and very into the class. It took me up to the last two submissions to figure it out. Words can't describe the scope of class. He wants to teach you how to think and think critically of anything and everything. Class discussions are fun and I genuinely enjoyed the learning and work aspects of class.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: He cared more about students engaging and trying to learn than he did about grades, & he was always happy to help or explain something. However, he talked a ton about stuff I knew nothing about, which was not fun to deal with in a 481 class. If you're unfamiliar with rhetoric/philosophy, I would not recommend him for a 481, but otherwise he's great
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Though you could tell he passionate about the history of rhetoric, the lectures were confusing and boring. There were three essays/exams that were unnecessarily long and difficult. Also, there were multiple discussion posts per week. All in all, too much work and not enough clarification. Good at emailing back, though.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He's a very nice professor, but the grading is very heavy. Often, it is unclear what he asks for in heavy papers which can lead you to feel very stressed and do poorly. He tries to help you when there is a misunderstanding, but the dude can come off as too smart to effectively make you understand what he is trying to say.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: You have four papers that arent worth much and three that are unit papers that are worth a bit more. You have to read and know the material in order to write the way he wants you to. He pushes you to be better and though Ive appreciated this he graded hard. Your grade depends on these seven papers only so do well.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. DiCaglio is very knowledgable and you can tell he is intelligent. With that being said, knowing information is different than teaching information. I had him for a mandatory english and it was the most difficult class I have taken in college as of yet. From the first day up until when I had to drop the course, I had no idea what was going on.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. DiCaglio is really nice and knowledgeable. I learned a lot of real-world practical skills from him and left his class with way more editing experience than I thought I would. The class consists of three major projects that aren't too bad if you stay on top of weekly assignments. He expects you to put in a lot hard work, but rewards you for it.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He does talk in a way that goes beyond your head which can be challenging at times. However, his class itself it fairly easy to manage. 2 discussion posts a week over lectures, 3 experiments, and 3 tests. He's a really nice and understanding guy if you just show him you're putting in effort!
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a very intelligent man, no questions there. Lectures and conversations go over students' heads and he does no work to bring it back down. Really discouraging and is hard to take risks in class without him shooting you down. Don't talk about God with him. If anything he's taught me not to get hurt by negative and critical comments
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I honestly disliked everything about this class. Dr. DiCaglio assigned us seven science fiction novels to read in seven weeks. The novels were really weird and our papers did not have clear guidelines at all. In the end, I believe that I learned a little about writing, but overall, I hated attending class because lectures were so scattered.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: DiCaglio is an awesome prof. A lot of my classmates did not enjoy the class because he does expect work put into your assignments. There were a few main projects and only 1 test that he lets you take multiple times until you make an 80 or above. He's a bit tough in his grading, but I left the class with so much editing experience under my belt!
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Dicaglio seems to be laid back, but when it comes to projects, if you don't edit like you have 10 years of PhD- level experience, you probably won't get an A. He gives a lot of feedback, but much of it is how many ways you were wrong. His grading scale is subject to change whenever and, in my opinion, arbitrary with no real project rubrics.
reviews.ratingTags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: This class is project-oriented. By the end of the class, you will leave feeling you actually gained some real-world editing skills. A lot of people thought he was a tough grader, but I think it's only because he's not very clear with his grading criteria. However, he does provide great feedback. Definitely not an easy A, but would recommend.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed learning the actual editing process, but I was surprised by the way we all were graded. Our first big project was worth 30% of our final grade, and it was graded as if we should be experts already, when we are really very new to editing. The final group project was helpful but a lot more work than any of my other classes.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Josh seems like this super laid back guy in class, but as soon as you get back your first small or large project, it hits you how tough he is with grading. It seems pretty arbitrary to be honest. If you didn't find something that he did, you lose points. Definitely not the chill guy he wants  you to think he is. I wouldn't take another class by him
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Very enthusiastic- you can tell he's passionate about what he teaches. BUT, he grades pretty harshly. Even if you put in 110% effort into a project, he'll take off points if you didn't do things exactly the way he would have done them. Very nit-picky. There were 2 main projects to the course, both of which were  overwhelming (and stressful).
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS
